units.la: Pars prominentior tuberculi instar ex osse procedens ἐπίφυσις[?] & processus dicitur.
units.tr: A more prominent part that projects from the bone like a small knob is called the epiphysis [ἐπίφυσις] or process.

units.la: Pars alterius ossis cavum subiens, Caput dicitur Cavum seu sinus ossis est, qui alterius ossis caput excipit.
units.tr: The part of one bone that enters a hollow is called the head. The hollow, or socket, of a bone is that which receives the head of another bone.

units.la: Hic si fuerit amplus, acetabuli nomen accipit.
units.tr: If this is large, it takes the name acetabulum.

units.la: Pars ossis & processus gracilior capiti praemissus collum seu cervix ossis dicitur.
units.tr: The narrower part of a bone and process placed in front of the head is called the neck or cervix of the bone.

units.la: Conjunctio ossium inter se qua conjunguntur, est vel articulatio, vel συμφυσις[?].
units.tr: The joining of bones with one another, by which they are connected, is either articulation or symphysis [συμφυσις].

units.la: Articulatio est ossium compositio, inserviens motui.
units.tr: Articulation is the composition of bones, serving motion.

units.la: Estq; Diarthrosis, vel Synarthrosis.
units.tr: It is either diarthrosis or synarthrosis.

units.la: Diarthrosis est articulatio ad motum manifestum.
units.tr: Diarthrosis is articulation for evident motion.

units.la: Ea est vel Enarthrosis, vel Arthrodia, vel Ginglymos.
units.tr: This is either enarthrosis, or arthrodia, or ginglymus.

units.la: Enarthrosis est ubi rotundum aut ob-longum caput in sinum aliquem inseri-tur.
units.tr: Enarthrosis is where a round or oblong head is inserted into some hollow.

units.la: Arthrodia est, quae leniter cavum in superficie & capitulum etiam depressum habet.
units.tr: Arthrodia is that which has a gently hollowed surface and a slightly depressed little head.

units.la: Ginglymos est, in qua ossa sese invicem ingrediuntur, & cum suscipiunt, tum suscipiuntur.
units.tr: Ginglymus is that in which the bones fit into one another, both receiving and being received.

units.la: Synarthrosis est coarticulatio ossium ad motum obscurum : Ea autem similiter est Enarthrosis, Arthrodia, & Symphysis.
units.tr: Synarthrosis is the joining of bones for obscure motion. This too is similarly of the kinds enarthrosis, arthrodia and symphysis.

units.la: Symphysis est ossium inter se unio sine motu.
units.tr: Symphysis is the union of bones with one another without motion.

units.la: Estque Sutura, vel Gomphosis, vel Harmonia.
units.tr: It is either suture, or gomphosis, or harmonia.

units.la: Sutura est ossium Symphysis in modum serrae, unius dente in alterius sinum subeunte facta.
units.tr: Suture is a symphysis of bones made like a saw, one tooth entering the recess of another.

units.la: Gomphosis est ossium Symphysis, qua instar clavi ossi infigitur.
units.tr: Gomphosis is a symphysis of bones, in which one is fixed into the bone like a nail.

units.la: Harmonia est ossium Symphysis, facta per simplicem lineam.
units.tr: Harmonia is a symphysis of bones, made by a simple line.

units.la: CAPUT XXXII. OSTEOLOGIAM ET HUMANORUM OSSIUM SCELETON speciatim exponens. SECTIO PRIMA. DE OSSIBUS CRANII.
units.tr: CHAPTER 32. A SPECIFIC ACCOUNT OF OSTEOLOGY AND THE SKELETON OF THE HUMAN BONES. SECTION 1. ON THE BONES OF THE SKULL.

units.la: Hactenus in genere de ossium partibus & conjunctione: nunc de ossium speciebus, seu humana Osteologia & Sceleto speciatim dispici-emus.
units.tr: So far we have dealt in general with the parts of the bones and their joining. Now let us examine, in particular, the kinds of bones, that is, human osteology and the skeleton.

units.la: O S ergo est Capitis vel Trunci.
units.tr: The bone, then, is either of the head or of the trunk.

units.la: Os capitis est, quod capitis fabricam sustinet & munit.
units.tr: The bone of the head is that which supports and protects the structure of the head.

units.la: Excipies à sustentatione & munitione dentes, ossicula auditoria, & alia pauca.
units.tr: Excepted from this support and protection are the teeth, the little bones of hearing, and a few others.

units.la: Os capitis est Cranium vel Maxilla.
units.tr: The bone of the head is either the cranium or the jaw.

units.la: Cranium seu Calvaria est os capitis, cerebrum continens & communiens.
units.tr: The cranium, or skull-cap, is the bone of the head that contains and encloses the brain.

units.la: Os cranii est Externum vel Internum.
units.tr: The bone of the cranium is either external or internal.

units.la: Externum est, quod externe magis munit & circumvallat.
units.tr: The external bone is that which protects and walls in the outside more.

units.la: Estq; duorum generum: Primum genus complectitur ossa syncipitis & occipitis; Alterum vero ossa frontis & temporum.
units.tr: It is of two kinds. The first kind comprises the bones of the crown and the back of the head; the second, the bones of the forehead and the temples.

units.la: De Suturis.
units.tr: On the Sutures.

units.la: Hæc externa cranii ossa committuntur & distinguuntur futuris.
units.tr: These external bones of the cranium are joined and separated by sutures.

units.la: Sutura cranii est vera vel spuria.
units.tr: A suture of the cranium is either true or false.

units.la: Vera sutura est, quæ manifeste est serratilis, & dentatis inter se pectinatim compagibus coit.
units.tr: A true suture is one that is plainly serrated, and joins with teeth-like fittings meshing together like a comb.

units.la: Vera est recta vel obliqua.
units.tr: A true suture is either straight or oblique.

units.la: Recta est Sagittalis, quæ per verticem recta incedit, & quodammodo parpartem calvariæ dextram à sinistra di-stinguit.
units.tr: The straight one is the sagittal, which runs straight over the top of the head and, in a way, divides the right half of the skull from the left.

units.la: Obliqua est Coronalis, vel Lamdo-eides.
units.tr: The oblique ones are the coronal and the lambdoid.

units.la: Coronalis in syncipite transversim sita est, anteriorem circa frontem circuli speciem ambiens, & ossa syncipitis ab osse frontis dirimens.
units.tr: The coronal suture lies crosswise on the crown of the head, curving around the front like a circle, and separates the bones of the crown from the frontal bone.

units.la: Lamdoeides in occipitio vergit adu-tramq; aurem, quæ divulsa in ipso ascensu angustior fit, & in cuneum coit, distinquens ossa syncipitis & temporum, ab osse occipitis.
units.tr: The lambdoid suture runs at the back of the head towards each ear; it is spread apart, but as it rises it becomes narrower and comes together in a wedge, separating the bones of the crown and the temples from the occipital bone.

units.la: Mendosæ vel Spuriæ (Hippocrati squamo-sæ agglutinationes) sunt obscurè serratiles, & utrinq; in temporibus singulæ, unde temporales futuræ dictæ.
units.tr: The false or spurious sutures (which Hippocrates called squamous joints) are obscurely serrated, and there is one on each side at the temples; hence they are called the temporal sutures.

units.la: Hæc de futuris cranii exterioris: jam ordine de syncipitis & occipitis ossibus.
units.tr: So much for the sutures of the outer cranium. Now, in order, the bones of the crown and the back of the head.

units.la: Syncipitis os dicitur Bregma, quod est os syncipitis superiorisq; cranii. Hujus ossis partes duę sunt, utrinque in capitis lateribus una: unde Parietalia & verticis ossa dicuntur.
units.tr: The bone of the crown is called the bregma, which is the bone of the crown and the upper part of the skull. This bone has two parts, one on each side of the head; hence they are called the parietal bones, or the bones of the vertex.

units.la: Occipitis os est, quod in occipitio constat partibus inæqualibus, aliis crassioribus, aliis vero tenuioribus.
units.tr: The occipital bone is that which, at the back of the head, consists of unequal parts, some thicker and some thinner.

units.la: Hoc os in adultis unicum, in pueris ex pluribus constructum cernitur.
units.tr: In adults this bone is seen as one; in children it is seen to be built of several pieces.

units.la: In infima hujus ossis parte ad magni foraminis latera duo conspiciuntur capita, quæ primæ vertebræ finibus inarti-culantur, cujus articulationis beneficio caput motu proprio in anteriorem & posteriorem partem nutat.
units.tr: On the lowest part of this bone, at either side of the great foramen, two heads are seen, which are jointed to the ends of the first vertebra. By the benefit of this joint the head nods on its own motion forwards and backwards.

units.la: Os frontis est unicum in anteriori parte capitis seu fronte, a syncipite & cavis temporum per medias oculorum sedes, ad summum usq; nasum perreptans.
units.tr: The frontal bone is single, at the front of the head or forehead, running from the crown and the hollows of the temples through the middle of the eye sockets, as far as the top of the nose.

units.la: Huius ossis cum est processus, tum sinus.
units.tr: This bone has both a process and a sinus.

units.la: Processus hic longus est, utrunque ad capitis latus densus ac durus, qui alteri simili processui ex maxilla superiore pro deunti[?] occurrens, Os jugale, vulgo Os paris constituit.
units.tr: The process is long, dense and hard on each side of the head, and where it meets a similar process of the upper jaw it forms the zygomatic bone, commonly called the cheekbone.

units.la: Os igitur jugale nulla est propria circumscriptione terminatum, sed ex duobus processibus oppositis obliqua futurâ coeuntibus conflatum.
units.tr: The zygomatic bone is therefore not bounded by any one proper outline, but is formed from two opposed processes joined by an oblique suture.

units.la: Sinus ossis frontis est supra supercilia amplus ad dextram & sinistram vergens, in quo dicitur aer recipi & servari.
units.tr: The sinus of the frontal bone is a wide cavity above the eyebrows, extending to the right and left, in which air is said to be received and kept.

units.la: Temporum ossa duo sunt, utrinque unum ad suam aurem positum, tortuolam habens insculptam cavitatem, auditus gratia.
units.tr: There are two temporal bones, one placed on each side by its ear, having a twisting cavity carved into it for the sake of hearing.

units.la: Horum processus numerantur quatuor.
units.tr: Four processes of these are counted.

units.la: 1. Mammillaris qui rupis seu vaccini uberis similitudinem refert, deservicns musculorum insertioni, & relinques amplam sedem auditus organis.
units.tr: (1) The mammillary process, which resembles a nipple or a cow's udder, serves for the insertion of muscles and leaves a broad seat for the organs of hearing.

units.la: 2. Styloeides seu Graphoeides à styli scriptorii similitudine dictus, in hujus ossis basin implantatus, pertenuis, longus & durus.
units.tr: (2) The styloid, or graphoid, process, named from its likeness to a writing stylus, is implanted in the base of this bone; it is very slender, long and hard.

units.la: 3. Tertius juxta Styloeidem in longum protuberat, interiori parti labyrinthus reflectendis aëris ictibus appositus.
units.tr: (3) The third process projects lengthwise beside the styloid, placed to turn back the blows of air against the inner part of the labyrinth.

units.la: 4. Quartus est portio jugalis ossis ab auris meatu incipiens, & in primum maxillae superioris definens.
units.tr: (4) The fourth is the zygomatic part of the bone, beginning at the passage of the ear and ending at the first part of the upper jaw.

units.la: Adhuc externum cranii os: Internum est, quod magis intra capitis substantiam collocatum est.
units.tr: So far the external bone of the cranium. The internal bone is that which lies more within the substance of the head.

units.la: Hoc inservit vel membro, vel sensui.
units.tr: This serves either a member or a sense.

units.la: Membro internum os serviens est cerebri, vel linguae.
units.tr: The internal bone serving a member is that of the brain or of the tongue.

units.la: Cerebro inserviens os dicitur Basilare, quod substratum cerebro basis quasi i-psius est.
units.tr: The bone serving the brain is called the basilar, which lies beneath the brain and is, as it were, its base.

units.la: Dicitur Sphenoeides, id est, cuneale seu cuneiforme, quod instar cunei inter maxillam superiorem & os frontis sit impactum.
units.tr: It is called sphenoid, that is, wedge-shaped or cuneiform, because it is fixed like a wedge between the upper jaw and the frontal bone.

units.la: In hoc osse est cùm sinus, tùm processus.
units.tr: This bone has both sinuses and processes.

units.la: Sinus est in internæ calvariæ medio, equi sellæ similimus, in quo sita solet esse glandula pituitam suscipiens, è qua postea defluit in palatum & nares.
units.tr: The sinus lies in the middle of the inner skull, very like a horse's saddle; in it is usually placed a gland which receives phlegm, from which it afterwards flows down into the palate and the nostrils.

units.la: Processus sphenoeides sunt gemini ea parte, quæ cohæret cum extrema maxilla superiore, ubi molares infixi, ad calvariæ basin: Dicuntur Pterygoeides: quia exprimunt alarum vespertilionum effigiem.
units.tr: The sphenoid processes are two, in the part that joins the extreme end of the upper jaw, where the molars are set, at the base of the skull. They are called pterygoid, because they represent the shape of a bat's wings.

units.la: Lingua inserviens os dicitur Hyoeides vel ypsiloeides, estque os anteriore parte, qua os respicit in valdè obtusum angulum convexum, & linguæ insertionem suscipiens, posteriore parte, quâ ad fauces vergit, concavum.
units.tr: The bone serving the tongue is called hyoid or upsiloid. Its front part, which faces the jaw, forms a very blunt, convex angle, and it receives the attachment of the tongue; its back part, which turns towards the throat, is concave.

units.la: Sensui inserviens seu sensui alicui certo destinatum, est vel olfactui vel auditui.
units.tr: The bone serving a sense, or destined for a particular sense, is for either smell or hearing.

units.la: Olfactui subserviens os dicitur Ethmoci-des seu Cribriforme, quod multis foraminulis seu cribri instar pervium, ut per ea patere possit ascensus odoribus cerebrum petentibus.
units.tr: The bone serving smell is called ethmoid, or cribriform, because it is pierced with many tiny foramina, like a sieve, so that the odours seeking the brain may have a passage up through them.

units.la: Ethmoeidis est processus alius & subtilis in media ejus regione prominens, sedem utramq; intersecans, qua olfactus instrumenta sita sunt, quiq; in nares descendens, nasi septum constituit.
units.tr: The ethmoid bone has another fine process projecting in the middle of its region, which divides the seat on either side; in it the instruments of smell are placed, and it descends into the nostrils and forms the septum of the nose.

units.la: Auditui subserviens os triplex est, Malleus, Incus & Stapha seu stapes.
units.tr: The bone serving hearing is threefold: the malleus, the incus, and the stapes, or stapha.

units.la: Malleus est ossiculum, quod parte superiore est capite oblongo & rotundo, parte inferiore mucronis instar in acutum tendit; hac inseritur in membranulam, quae eam ipsam tympani instar quatit.
units.tr: The malleus is a little bone which, in its upper part, has a long, round head, and in its lower part tapers to a point like a spike; this is inserted into a small membrane, which it shakes like a drum.

units.la: Incus est alterum auditus ossiculum, parte superiore crassiusculum, qua planam incudis formam refert, quasi excipiat ictus permoti malleoli.
units.tr: The incus is the other little bone of hearing; its upper part is somewhat thick, and there it resembles the flat form of an anvil, as if to receive the blows of the malleolus when it is moved.

units.la: Stapha seu Stapeda est tertium ossiculum intra tympanum triangulare, & in medio perforatum, speciem soni admittens.
units.tr: The stapes, or stapeda, is the third little bone, triangular within the tympanum and pierced in the middle, so as to admit the sound.

units.la: SECTIO II. DE MAXILLIS ET DENTIBUS.
units.tr: SECTION II. ON THE JAWS AND TEETH.

units.la: Hactenus Cranium : Maxilla est os capitis, quod ex multis constans ossibus, alveos & sinus dentium continet.
units.tr: So far the skull. The jaw is the bone of the head which, made up of many bones, contains the sockets and cavities of the teeth.

units.la: Estque superior & inferior.
units.tr: There is an upper and a lower jaw.

units.la: Superior est maxilla immobilis, duodecim (vel tredecim numerante Columbo) ossiculorum, cranio annexa.
units.tr: The upper jaw is immovable, made of twelve (or, as Columbus counts, thirteen) small bones, joined to the skull.

units.la: Ossa maxillae superioris committuntur per Symphysin harmonicam.
units.tr: The bones of the upper jaw are joined by harmonic suture.

units.la: Inferior est maxilla mobilis unici tantum & continui ossis, superiori maxillae parte posteriori innexa.
units.tr: The lower jaw is movable, consisting of one single continuous bone, attached to the back part of the upper jaw.

units.la: Haec in duos processus utrinq; desinit: prior tendit in mucronem acute excipiens temporalis musculi tendinem.
units.tr: This ends in two processes on each side. The anterior one tapers to a sharp point and receives the tendon of the temporal muscle.

units.la: Posterior capitulum & cervicem habet, & cum temporum osse inter jugalis radicem & foramen auditorium articulatur.
units.tr: The posterior one has a head and a neck, and is jointed with the temporal bone between the root of the cheekbone and the auditory foramen.

units.la: Harum duarum maxillarum alveis inseruntur Dentes.
units.tr: The teeth are set in the sockets of these two jaws.

units.la: Dentes igitur sunt ossa, maxillarum alveis ordine inserta, comminuendo cibo praecipue destinata.
units.tr: Teeth, then, are bones set in order in the sockets of the jaws, destined chiefly for grinding food.

units.la: Horum pars est cùm superior seu truncus, tùm inferior seu radix.
units.tr: Each tooth has an upper part, or crown, and a lower part, or root.

units.la: Truncus seu caput dentis est pars extra sinum maxillæ eminens, nonsentiens [?].
units.tr: The crown or head of the tooth is the part that projects outside the socket of the jaw, not sensing [?].

units.la: Radix est dentis inferior pars, quæ alveo maxillæ inserta, infigitur acutè, per nervos sibi implantatos sentiens.
units.tr: The root is the lower part of the tooth, which is set in the socket of the jaw and fixed firmly there, sensing through the nerves implanted in it.

units.la: DENTES articulantur maxillis per Gomphosin mediante carne.
units.tr: Teeth are joined to the jaws by gomphosis, with flesh intervening.

units.la: DENTES utrobiq; seu in utraq; maxilla sunt anteriores, vel posteriores.
units.tr: In each jaw the teeth are either anterior or posterior.

units.la: Anteriores habent radicem unam, suntq; incisorii vel canini.
units.tr: The anterior teeth have one root, and they are incisors or canines.

units.la: Incisorii sunt anteriores acuti & lati, oblatum cibum mordendo promte incidentes.
units.tr: The incisors are the front teeth, sharp and broad, quick to cut the food offered by biting.

units.la: Dicuntur & Gelasini quod inter ridendum nudati ostendantur.
units.tr: They are also called gelasini, because they show when the lips are drawn back in laughing.

units.la: Canini sunt bini utrobiq; latere incisoriis proximi, exertis canum dentibus persimiles.
units.tr: The canines are two on each side, next to the incisors, very like the projecting teeth of dogs.

units.la: Posteriores habent radices una plures; suntq; utrobiq; maxillares seu molares, & genuini seu sophronisteres.
units.tr: The posterior teeth have one or more roots. On each side they are either maxillary or molar teeth, and genuine or sophronisteres (wisdom teeth).

units.la: Maxillares seu molares sunt posteriores proximi, quini ab utroq; latere, quibus ceu molis cibi atteruntur. Genuini seu sapientiae dentes sunt omnium postremi, gingiva fere operti, post annos tandem pubertatis erumpentes.
units.tr: The maxillary or molar teeth are the back teeth nearest the front, five on each side, by which food is ground down as if into a mass. The genuine or wisdom teeth are the last of all, almost wholly covered by the gum, and they erupt only after the years of puberty have passed.

units.la: SECTIO III. DE OSSIBUS PE-CTORIS.
units.tr: SECTION III. ON THE BONES OF THE CHEST.

units.la: Hactenus de ossibus capitis: Trunci ossa sunt, quae truncum sustinent & muniunt.
units.tr: So far concerning the bones of the head. The bones of the trunk are those which support and protect the trunk.

units.la: Trunci ossa sunt medii, vel extremi.
units.tr: The bones of the trunk are either middle or extreme.

units.la: Medii truncum medium firmant.
units.tr: The middle ones firm up the middle of the trunk.

units.la: Suntq; vel anteriora vel posteriora.
units.tr: And they are either anterior or posterior.

units.la: Anterius os trunci est Os pectoris, totum pectus instar scuti muniens: Graecis dicitur στέρνον.
units.tr: The anterior bone of the trunk is the breastbone, which protects the whole chest like a shield; in Greek it is called sternon [στέρνον].

units.la: Estq; in pueris quatuor partium seu ossiculorum: in adultis trium; uniuntur autem invicem mediante cartilagine per symphysin.
units.tr: In children it consists of four parts or small bones; in adults of three. These are joined to one another by means of cartilage, through symphysis.

units.la: Primum ac supremum est latum, & quasi triangulare, supernè instar mediae lunae cavatum.
units.tr: The first and uppermost part is broad and somewhat triangular, hollowed on its upper side like a half-moon.

units.la: Medium est paulo tenuius.
units.tr: The middle part is a little thinner.

units.la: Infimum in cartilaginem desinés, dicunt malum Granatum, vel Os Xipho-cides, ensiforme.
units.tr: The lowest part ends in cartilage; they call it the pomegranate bone, or the xiphoid bone, sword-shaped.

units.la: SECTIO IV. DE OSSIBVS DORSI.
units.tr: SECTION IV. CONCERNING THE BONES OF THE BACK.

units.la: Posteriora medii trunci ossa sunt ossa Dorsi.
units.tr: The bones of the trunk's middle part that lie behind are the bones of the back.

units.la: Dorsum dicitur id, quod à basi occipitis ad ipsum pertingit anum.
units.tr: The back is that which reaches from the base of the occiput down to the anus itself.

units.la: Dorsi ossa sunt vertebrata, quae vertebris constant.
units.tr: The bones of the back are vertebrated bones, made up of vertebrae.

units.la: Vertebrae seu spondyli sunt ossa dorsi in crassiores nodos conglobata, in medio cava, spinalem medullam continentia.
units.tr: Vertebrae, or spondyli, are the bones of the back gathered into thicker knots, hollow in the middle and containing the spinal marrow.

units.la: Vertebrae partes sunt corpus ipsum & processus.
units.tr: A vertebra has two parts: the body itself and the processes.

units.la: Corpus est ipsa pars quasi corpulenta vertebrae.
units.tr: The body is the part of the vertebra that is, as it were, its bulk.

units.la: Processus est ea pars, quae in corpore quolibet loco protuberat.
units.tr: A process is that part which protrudes from the body at any point.

units.la: Intra utrumq; est foramen dorsali medullae tuendae paratum.
units.tr: Between both there is a foramen, prepared for protecting the dorsal marrow.

units.la: Os totum vertebratum generaliter dicitur Spina dorsi: quae est os posterius trunci medii viginti quatuor varie invicem articulatis constans vertebris, ad motū flexionis & erectionis appositum.
units.tr: The whole jointed bone is generally called the spine of the back. It is the hinder bone of the middle trunk, consisting of twenty-four vertebrae variously jointed with one another, and fitted for the movements of bending and straightening.

units.la: Ossa seu spina dorsi est superior vel In-ferior.
units.tr: The bones or spine of the back are either upper or lower.

units.la: Superiora offa dorsi sunt cervicis vel thoracis.
units.tr: The upper bones of the back are those of the neck or of the chest.

units.la: Offa Cervicus seu colli sunt pars spinae seu dorsi superior, septem vertebrarum graciliorum ampliorem cavitatem habentium, in quarum suprema articulatione caput antrorsum & retrorsum fle-ctitur.
units.tr: The bones of the neck, or of the throat, are the upper part of the spine or back: seven slender vertebrae with a wider cavity, at whose uppermost joint the head is bent forward and backward.

units.la: Thoracis offa sunt pars spinae longior, infra colli vertebras paulo pedetentim majoribꝰ vertebris duodecim constans.
units.tr: The bones of the chest are the longer part of the spine, lying below the vertebrae of the neck, gradually a little larger, consisting of twelve vertebrae.

units.la: Corpora vertebrarum thoracis sunt rari-ora & fungosiora, in medio protuberan-tia, & in rotundum adducta, exceptis primis duabus, sunt itidem supra infra-que fere plana, & multam interjectam habent cartilaginem.
units.tr: The bodies of the vertebrae of the chest are rarer and more spongy, protuberant in the middle and drawn into a round shape; except the first two, they are likewise nearly flat above and below, and have a considerable cartilage interposed.

units.la: Sunt etiam quinis appendicibus donata.
units.tr: They are also furnished with five appendages.

units.la: Inferiora offa dorsi sunt manifestarum vertebrarum, & obscurarum seu quasi vertebrarum.
units.tr: The lower bones of the back are those of the distinct vertebrae and those of the obscure, or as it were, vertebrae.

units.la: Manifestorum spondylorum os est os lum-borum, quod est inferior pars dorsi in-fra thoracis spondylos, constans omnium maximis, rarissimis, & crebris fo-raminibus, perviis vertebris quinq;
units.tr: The bone of the distinct vertebrae is the bone of the loins, which is the lower part of the back below the vertebrae of the chest, consisting of the largest, very rare and frequent foramina, five vertebrae passable.

units.la: Harum vertebrarum processus superiores sinus speciem referunt; Inferiores in hos immittendi, paululum prominent, & ita sua ipsi cartilagine committun-tur.
units.tr: The upper processes of these vertebrae resemble a sinus; the lower ones, to be inserted into these, project a little, and so are joined to them by their own cartilage.

units.la: Transversi processus sunt longiores, tenuiores, & inter se dispares.
units.tr: The transverse processes are longer, thinner, and unequal among themselves.

units.la: Posteriores processus validi sunt crassi, lati, & in extremitate circulari linea de-finiti.
units.tr: The posterior processes are strong, thick, broad, and defined at the extremity by a circular line.

units.la: Harum denique vertebrarum appendi-ces quanto caeteras magnitudine ante-cellunt, tanto etiam majorem & crassi-orem cartilaginem adeptæ sunt.
units.tr: Lastly, the appendages of these vertebrae, as much as they surpass the others in size, so also have they acquired a larger and thicker cartilage.

units.la: Obscurorum seu quasi spondylorum inferiora ossa dorsi sunt Os sacrum, & Coccy-gis.
units.tr: The lower bones of the back, of the obscure or as it were vertebrae, are the sacrum and the coccyx.

units.la: Os sacrum est infra lumborum vertebras latum & magnum, ex quinque vel sex ossibus seu vertebris obscure distinctis conflatum, immobile, super quo superiora omnia superstructa, & inferio-ra substrata moventur.
units.tr: The sacrum lies below the vertebrae of the loins, broad and large, formed from five or six bones or vertebrae obscurely distinguished, immovable, upon which all the upper parts are built and the lower parts are placed beneath and moved.

units.la: Partes hujus sacri ossis in tenera ætate licet possint laxari & separari; in adultis tamen ita coalescunt, ut vix separari possint. Os sacrum ad latera, ante & retro, est perforatum: estque anteriore parte leve & sinuum, posteriore gibbum.
units.tr: The parts of this sacred bone can be loosened and separated in tender age; in adults, however, they grow together so that they can scarcely be separated. The sacrum is perforated at the sides, before and behind; it is smooth and hollowed on the front part, and humped on the back.

units.la: Ossis hujus cùm sunt processus, tùm etiam sinus in extimis trium ossium superiorum lateribus, quorum medius major & profundior.
units.tr: Of this bone there are processes as well as sinuses on the outer sides of the three upper bones, of which the middle one is larger and deeper.

units.la: Os coccygis est ultima dorsi portio ex quatuor ossiculis constructa, ab ossis sacri extremitate velut cauda pendens.
units.tr: The coccyx is the last portion of the back, constructed of four small bones, hanging from the end of the sacrum like a tail.

units.la: Primum ossiculum coccygis reliquis est latius & majus, superne sinum habens, quo imam postremi sacri ossis partem excipit.
units.tr: The first small bone of the coccyx is broader and larger than the rest, having above a sinus by which it receives the lowest part of the last bone of the sacrum.

units.la: Reliqua tria rotunda quodammodo sunt, & in acutum tendunt.
units.tr: The remaining three are in a sense round, and taper to a point.

units.la: Putatur os coccygis à sacro laxari & versus posteriora flecti, cum mulieres foetum emittunt.
units.tr: It is thought that the coccyx is loosened from the sacrum and bent backward when women bring forth their young.

units.la: SECTIO V. DE COSTIS.
units.tr: SECTION V. OF THE RIBS.

units.la: Hæc de ossibus pectoris & dorsi, inter quæ interseruntur utrinque lateralia ossa, quæ dicuntur
units.tr: These are the bones of the breast and back, between which the lateral bones lie on either side, which are called

units.la: Costæ sunt ossa lateralia semicircularia, vertebris thoracis singulis bina validissimè inarticulata ac implantata, suo amplexu viscera & intestina continentia.
units.tr: The ribs are the lateral semicircular bones. Each is attached to a thoracic vertebra by two very strong joints, and they enclose the viscera and intestines in their embrace.

units.la: Costæ versus dorsum, & partem posteriorem rem duriores sunt & solidiores, versus thoracem & anteriorem partem paulò molliores & spongiosiores evadunt: tandem verò in cartilagines desinunt.
units.tr: The ribs toward the back and the posterior part are harder and more solid, while toward the chest and the front they become somewhat softer and more spongy. Finally, they end in cartilage.

units.la: Costæ sunt veræ seu legitimæ, vel spuriæ seu mendosæ.
units.tr: Ribs are either true (genuine, legitimate) or false (spurious, defective).

units.la: Veræ costæ sunt superiores septem, ampliores, ossi pectoris insertæ, & thoracem claudentes.
units.tr: True ribs are the upper seven, which are larger, joined to the breastbone, and close off the chest.

units.la: Hæ cum pectoris osse committuntur per cartilaginem.
units.tr: These are joined to the breastbone by cartilage.

units.la: Spuriæ costæ sunt quinq; inferiores, æquè minores, pectoris ossi non commissæ, neq; thoracem claudentes.
units.tr: False ribs are the lower five, which are also smaller. They are not joined to the breastbone and do not close off the chest.

units.la: Hæ molliores sunt & laxius cohærent, unde quidam appellant χόνδρος[?], & partes ventris iis subjectas ὑποχόνδρια[?].
units.tr: These are softer and cohere more loosely, whence some call them [χόνδρος], and the parts of the belly lying beneath them [ὑποχόνδρια].

units.la: SECTIO VI. DE SCAPVLIS ET CLA-VICVLIS.
units.tr: SECTION VI. ON THE SHOULDER-BLADES AND COLLARBONES.

units.la: Sic ossa medii trunci fuerunt: Extremi trunci ossa sunt, quae a medio trunco utrinque instar ramorum propendent.
units.tr: Such were the bones of the middle trunk. The bones of the extremities of the trunk are those which hang down on both sides from the middle trunk like branches.

units.la: Haec autem ossa excipiuntur excipiente osse.
units.tr: These bones are received by a receiving bone.

units.la: Suntque superiora vel inferiora.
units.tr: And they are either upper or lower.

units.la: Superiora extremi trunci ossa sunt, quae a suprema parte medii trunci utrinque enata prominent.
units.tr: The upper bones of the extremities of the trunk are those which project on both sides, sprouting from the uppermost part of the middle trunk.

units.la: Suntque ossa manuum.
units.tr: And these are the bones of the arms.

units.la: Manus hoc loco universe & late cum Hippocrate accipitur pro toto eo, quod a scapulis ad extremitatem usque digitorum porrigitur. Estque in utroque latere una, dextra & sinistra.
units.tr: Manus (the arm) is here taken broadly and generally, with Hippocrates, for the whole of what extends from the shoulder-blades to the tips of the fingers. There is one on each side, right and left.

units.la: Scapulae sunt ossa triquetra inaequalis crassitiei & tenuitatis, supra summis costis adhaerentia, manuumque ossa excipientia.
units.tr: Scapulae (shoulder-blades) are triangular bones of uneven thickness and thinness, attached to the uppermost ribs and receiving the bones of the arms.

units.la: Scapularum partes duae sunt, basis & cervix.
units.tr: The shoulder-blades have two parts: the base and the neck.

units.la: Basis scapularum est latus earum vertebris proximum, secundum dorsi longitudinem exporrectum.
units.tr: The base of the shoulder-blades is the side nearest the vertebrae, extending along the length of the back.

units.la: Cervix altera est scapularum pars valida, crassa & praedita oblongo sinu, brachium recipiente. Interna parte, quâ costas recipiunt, sunt cavæ; externâ verò gibbæ sunt & prominent.
units.tr: The neck is the other part of the shoulder-blade, strong and thick, provided with an oblong hollow that receives the arm. On the inner side, where they receive the ribs, they are hollow; on the outer side they are convex and project.

units.la: Scapularum deinde processus sunt, & appendices.
units.tr: Next are the processes and appendages of the shoulder-blades.

units.la: Processus tres sunt. 1. Est brevissimus in caput latù sinuatumq; desinens, excipiendo summo humero destinatus.
units.tr: There are three processes: (1) the shortest, ending in a broad, hollowed head, designed to receive the top of the shoulder;

units.la: 2. Est per quem brachium à costis diducitur ac distat, quiq; os humeri in suâ sede continet: dicitur q; Anchyroides.
units.tr: (2) the one by which the arm is drawn away and held apart from the ribs, and which keeps the humerus in its place; it is called Anchyroides;

units.la: 3. Est longior & prominentior, Græcis κορωνοειδὲς dictus, quasi humeri apex; cum hoc clavicula conjunguntur.
units.tr: (3) the longer and more prominent one, called koronoeides [κορωνοειδὲς] by the Greeks, as it were the apex of the shoulder; the clavicles are joined to this.

units.la: Appendices scapularum quinque sunt.
units.tr: There are five appendages of the shoulder-blades.

units.la: Harum tres ad latus internum juxta spinæ ductum ad basin adhærescunt.
units.tr: Three of these adhere to the inner side, near the base, along the course of the spine.

units.la: Reliquæ duæ ligamenta suggerunt, quibus vincitur humerus acetabulo & clavicula Acromio.
units.tr: The remaining two supply ligaments by which the humerus is bound to the socket and the clavicle to the acromion.

units.la: Scapulæ denique ossi pectoris uniuntur mediantibus claviculis, seu jugulis.
units.tr: Finally, the shoulder-blades are joined to the breastbone by means of the clavicles, or collarbones.

units.la: Claviculæ seu jugula sunt ossa fungosa, tenui crustâ tecta, fragilia, bis curvata, intrinsecus ad mediam usq; regionem cava:
units.tr: The clavicles, or jugula, are spongy bones covered with a thin crust, fragile, curved twice, and hollow inside as far as the middle region.

units.la: Clavicu-la. cava: Extrinsecus vero convexa protu-berant, scapulas distendentia, ne in tho-racem concidant.
units.tr: Outside, however, they are convex and protrude, holding the shoulder-blades apart so that they do not collapse into the chest.

units.la: Clavicularum cum sunt capita, tum appendices.
units.tr: The clavicles have both heads and appendages.

units.la: Capita duo; Primum est depressius, quo cum Acromii summitate conjun-gitur.*
units.tr: There are two heads. The first is lower, and by it the clavicle is joined to the summit of the acromion.

units.la: Alterum est rotundum, eaque parte sterni sinu recipitur.
units.tr: The other is round, and is received in that part by a hollow of the sternum.

units.la: Appendices utriq; parti assident suis obductæ cartilaginibus.
units.tr: The appendages sit on each side, covered with their own cartilages.

units.la: SECTIO VII. DE HUMERO ET CUBITO.
units.tr: SECTIO VII. ON THE HUMERUS AND ULNA.

units.la: Manuum ossa sunt cum Brachii, tum manus proprie dictæ.
units.tr: The bones of the hand are those of the arm as well as the hand properly so called.

units.la: Brachium est totus ossium ductus à scapulis ad manum pertingens.
units.tr: The arm is the whole structure of bones, extending from the shoulder-blades down to the hand.

units.la: Brachii ossa sunt humerus & cubitus.
units.tr: The bones of the arm are the humerus and the ulna.

units.la: Humerus est maximum brachii os, te-res & longum, parte superiore cum scapulæ osse, inferiore cum cubito conjunctum.
units.tr: The humerus is the largest bone of the arm, round and long, joined at its upper part to the shoulder-blade and at its lower part to the ulna.

units.la: Inferior pars ulnæ est, quæ levem radii sinum subiens, cum eo articulatur.
units.tr: The lower part of the ulna is the part that enters the small socket of the radius and is jointed with it.

units.la: Radius est os brevius & superius, paulo supra carpum definens ulnæ conjunctum.
units.tr: The radius is the shorter bone, lying uppermost, ending a little above the wrist and joined to the ulna.

units.la: Hujus caput superius minus & rotundius est, cum humero articulatum.
units.tr: Its upper head is smaller and rounder, and is jointed with the humerus.

units.la: Hoc deinde in cervicem descendit tenuem & oblongam, ad cujus extremitatem, quà vergit ad ulnam, tuberculum emittit.
units.tr: From there it descends into a slender, oblong neck, at the end of which, where it turns toward the ulna, it sends out a small tubercle.

units.la: Radius cum ulna componitur per Arthrodiam.
units.tr: The radius is joined with the ulna by arthrodia.

units.la: Inferius vero caput majus depressum & latum est, appendicis ope auctum.
units.tr: Its lower head, however, is larger, flattened and broad, and is enlarged by the aid of an appendage.

units.la: Hoc in superficie in amplum & geminum sinum excavatur, in quem inarticulantur duo postrema carpi ossa.
units.tr: On its surface it is hollowed into a wide, double socket, into which the two last bones of the carpus are jointed.

units.la: SECTIO VIII. DE CARPO, ET ME-TACARPIO.
units.tr: SECTION VIII. ON THE CARPUS AND METACARPUS.

units.la: Manus proprie dicta est organum δώσεως καὶ λήψεως.
units.tr: The hand, properly so called, is the organ of giving and receiving [δώσεως καὶ λήψεως].

units.la: Manus utriusq; offa sunt conjuncta, vel sejuncta.
units.tr: The bones of either hand are either joined or separated.

units.la: Conjuncta offa manus sunt, quæ ab o-mni parte intermediis vinculis conjun-ctæ cohærent.
units.tr: Joined bones of the hand are those which are connected by intermediate ligaments on every side.

units.la: Conjuncta manus offa sunt brachiale, seu Carpus, & postbrachiale, seu Metacarpion.
units.tr: The joined bones of the hand are the brachiale, or carpus, and the postbrachiale, or metacarpus.

units.la: Brachiale seu Carpus est os manus conjunctum comprehendens eam octo ossium struem, quae inter radium & metacarpium sita est.
units.tr: The brachiale, or carpus, is the joined bone of the hand, comprising the structure of eight bones, which lies between the radius and the metacarpus.

units.la: Carpi ossa duplici ordine juncta, duas veluti acies constituunt, primam & secundam. Utraq; est ossium quatuor.
units.tr: The bones of the carpus, joined in a double row, form two ridges, as it were, the first and the second. Each row consists of four bones.

units.la: Prima ossium acies parte superiore capiti radii ita committitur, ut primum secundumque ossiculum in sinum ipsius capitis inseratur, tertium paulum inhaerere videtur, quartum soli tertio annexum.
units.tr: The first row of bones is joined at the upper part to the head of the radius in such a way that the first and second little bones are inserted into the socket of that head, the third seems to rest only slightly, and the fourth is attached to the third alone.

units.la: Partes igitur humeri duae sunt: caput Superius & Inferius.
units.tr: The parts of the humerus, therefore, are two: the upper head and the lower head.

units.la: Superius est caput magnum & rotundum, in acetabulum scapulae insertum.
units.tr: The upper is a large, round head, inserted into the socket of the scapula.

units.la: Inferius in tria distincta & inaequalia velut capita exurgit, quibus conjungitur cubito.
units.tr: The lower rises into three distinct and unequal heads, as it were, by which it is joined to the cubit.

units.la: Humeri item est sinus, appendix, & processus.
units.tr: The humerus also has a sinus, an appendix, and a process.

units.la: Sinus est in medio inferiorum capitum prominentium ulnam sua sede continens.
units.tr: The sinus lies between the lower projecting heads and holds the ulna in its place.

units.la: Appendix est superioris capitis, vel inferioris.
units.tr: The appendix belongs to the upper head or the lower one.

units.la: Illa superiori capiti adnata, cartilaginea crusta oblita, in scapulæ acetabulum inseritur.
units.tr: The one belonging to the upper head, covered with a cartilaginous crust, is inserted into the socket of the scapula.

units.la: Hæc inferiori capiti adnata secundum Columbum; (negante Galeno & Valesio.)
units.tr: The one belonging to the lower head is, according to Columbus (Galen and Valsalva denying it), attached to it.

units.la: Processus duo sunt, ad utrumque latus inferioris partis, quibus hærent principia musculorum tendentium ad extremam manum.
units.tr: There are two processes, one on each side of the lower part, to which the origins of the muscles running to the outer hand are attached.

units.la: Cubitus est os inter humeri flexum & carpum in longum intercedens.
units.tr: The cubitus is the bone lying lengthwise between the bend of the humerus and the carpus.

units.la: Cubiti offa sunt ulna & radius.
units.tr: The bones of the cubit are the ulna and the radius.

units.la: Ulna est os cubiti maius, inferius ad latus parvi digiti porrectum à flexu ad carpum.
units.tr: The ulna is the larger bone of the cubit, lying on the side of the little finger, extending from the bend down to the carpus.

units.la: Ulnæ pars superior crassior est, in duos processus oblongos triangulares terminata.
units.tr: The upper part of the ulna is thicker and ends in two long triangular processes.

units.la: His processibus protuberantibus concluditur sinus Sigmoides, latinum C referens, quem processus isti comple-ctuntur, & circa illum vertuntur.
units.tr: These protruding processes enclose the sigmoid sinus, which resembles the Latin letter C; the processes grasp it and turn around it.

units.la: Hæc parte superiori articulatur cum humero per Ginglymon.
units.tr: By this upper part it is articulated with the humerus by a ginglymus.

units.la: A superiori parte ulna paulatim fit acclivis, & sensim attenuatur, usq; dum in caput & inferiorem partem desinat.
units.tr: From its upper part the ulna gradually slopes and tapers little by little, until it ends in a point and its lower part.

units.la: Secunda ossium acies parte posteriore cum postbrachiali articulatur, priore cum cæteris brachialis ossibus.
units.tr: The second row of bones is articulated at its back part with the postbrachiale, and at its front part with the other bones of the brachiale.

units.la: Hujus os primum ab interno latere versus pollicem occurrit: Secundum illi statim succedit: Tertium cum solo secundo cohærens, versus radium vergit; Quartum omnium minimum, uni tertio annectitur.
units.tr: The first of these bones meets the thumb on the inner side; the second follows immediately upon it; the third, cohering with the second alone, turns toward the radius; the fourth, the smallest of all, is joined to the third alone.

units.la: Ossa carpi cum radio per Diarthrosin, secum invicem per Synarthrosin, cum metacarpio partim per Synarthrosin, partim per Diarthrosin sunt conjuncta.
units.tr: The bones of the carpus are joined with the radius by diarthrosis, with one another by synarthrosis, and with the metacarpus partly by synarthrosis and partly by diarthrosis.

units.la: Metacarpiu seu postbrachiale est os manus conjunctum, continés quatuor ossa, supra cum carpo, infra cum quatuor primis digitorum ossibus articulata.
units.tr: The metacarpus, or postbrachiale, is the joined bone of the hand, containing four bones, articulated above with the carpus and below with the first bones of the four fingers.

units.la: Metacarpii ossa intus sunt sima[?], extrà verò gibba, infrà suprâq; appendicibus munita, ex quibꝰ ligamenta fluunt, quibꝰ ossa hæc inter se utrinq; convinciuntur.
units.tr: The bones of the metacarpus are hollow on the inner side, but convex on the outer side, and are furnished with appendages above and below, from which ligaments run, by which these bones are bound together on both sides.

units.la: Superiores appendices carpi ossibꝰ sinus præbent, Inferiores primis digitorum ossibꝰ capita exhibent.
units.tr: The upper appendages of the carpus provide sockets for the bones, and the lower ones offer heads to the first bones of the fingers.

units.la: Metacarpii autem ossa sunt vel longissima, vel paulatim breviora.
units.tr: The bones of the metacarpus, however, are either the longest or gradually shorter.

units.la: Longissimum metacarpii os est primum, digitum primum seu indicem sustinens.
units.tr: The longest bone of the metacarpus is the first, which supports the first finger, or index finger.

units.la: Paulatim breviora sunt tria reliqua.
units.tr: The three remaining bones are gradually shorter.

units.la: SECTIO IX. DE C[?]MANVS DIGITORVM OSSIBVS.
units.tr: SECTION IX. CONCERNING THE BONES OF THE HAND (MANUS) OF THE FINGERS

units.la: Sejuncta manus ossa sunt, quae utrinq; dissecta & soluta sunt.
units.tr: The bones of the hand are separated; they are cut and loosened on both sides.

units.la: Suntq; digitorum ossa externe curva ac teretia, interne plana vel quodammodo sima, internodiis distincta, digitos firmantia.
units.tr: The bones of the fingers are curved and rounded on the outside, flat or somewhat hollow on the inside, distinguished by joints, and they strengthen the fingers.

units.la: Quilibet digitus constat ternis seriatim constructis ossibus, totidemq; articulationibus.
units.tr: Each finger consists of three bones arranged in a row, and therefore of as many articulations.

units.la: Praeterea reperiuntur ossa σησαμοειδῆ, à sesamæ grani similitudine, nimiæ flexioni & laxationi occurrentia.
units.tr: Besides these, there are found the sesamoid bones, so called from their likeness to a grain of sesame, which lie at places of excessive bending and loosening.

units.la: Ossicula inter duos digitorum articulos contenta, Internodia dicuntur.
units.tr: The little bones contained between two joints of the fingers are called internodes.

units.la: Hæc internodia suscipiunt & suscipi-untur, ideoque articulantur per Enar-throsin.
units.tr: These internodes both receive and are received, and so they are jointed by enarthrosis.

units.la: Digitorum autem ossa articuli sunt vel magni vel parvi.
units.tr: The bones of the fingers, moreover, are joints, some large and some small.

units.la: Magni sunt articuli primi, singulorum digitorum quantitatis magnae.
units.tr: The large ones are the first joints of each finger, which are of large size.

units.la: Articuli primi committuntur vel brachialis, vel postbrachialis ossibus.
units.tr: The first joints are connected either to the brachial bones or to the postbrachial bones.

units.la: Articulus primus commissus brachiali est primum pollicis os.
units.tr: The first joint, connected to the brachial bone, is the first bone of the thumb.

units.la: Reliquorum digitorum articuli primi cum postbrachiali coarticulantur.
units.tr: The first joints of the remaining fingers are jointed with the postbrachial bone.

units.la: Parvi articuli digitorum sunt reliqui articuli digitorum, quantitatis parvae.
units.tr: The small joints of the fingers are the remaining joints of the fingers, of small size.

units.la: Eorum alii sunt minores, alii minimi.
units.tr: Of these, some are smaller and some are smallest.

units.la: Minores sunt secundi digitorum articuli.
units.tr: The smaller ones are the second joints of the fingers.

units.la: Minimi sunt tertii & extremi articuli.
units.tr: The smallest ones are the third and last joints.

units.la: SECTIO X. DE OSSE ILIUM, PUBIS, ET COXENDICIS.
units.tr: SECTION X. CONCERNING THE HIP-BONE, THE PUBIS, AND THE HIP-SOCKET.

units.la: Hactenus de ossibus superioribus extremae partis trunci: Inferiora sunt, quae ab ima medii trunci parte enata propen-dent, reliquum superius totum & ere-ctum gestantia.
units.tr: So far concerning the upper bones of the lower part of the trunk. The lower bones are those which, springing from the lowest part of the middle of the trunk, hang down, bearing the whole of the rest, which is upper and upright.

units.la: Suntq; ossa pedum, quae hic totam ossium struem à coxa ufq; ad extremum digitorum pedis notant.
units.tr: These are the bones of the feet, which here denote the whole structure of bones from the hip down to the tips of the toes.

units.la: Est autem pes in utroq; latere unus, dexter & sinister.
units.tr: There is indeed one foot on each side, right and left.

units.la: Pedes excipiens os est coxa,quod transver-sis sacri ossis procesfibꝰ commissum, inter illud & femur interjacet.
units.tr: The bone which receives the foot is the hip, which, joined to the transverse processes of the sacrum, lies between that and the thigh.

units.la: Hoc os est timembre, os ilium,os pu-bis, & os coxendicis.
units.tr: This bone is, in its three parts, the haunch-bone (os ilium), the pubic bone (os pubis), and the hip-socket bone (os coxendicis).

units.la: Os ilium est suprema coxæ pars latis-sima,qua cum osse sacro firmisima con-nexione conjungitur.
units.tr: The haunch-bone is the uppermost and broadest part of the hip, by which it is joined to the sacrum by a very firm connection.

units.la: Hoc parte posteriore duobus latis finibus infigitur, postrema parte semicirculari linea obducitur, quæ tota ap-pendice munitur.
units.tr: It is fixed by its posterior part at two broad edges, and its rear edge is traced by a semicircular line, which is strengthened along its whole length by an appendix.

units.la: Sinus ossis sacri tubera excipiunt: ap-pendices & partes eminentes ossis sacri sinus ingrediuntur.
units.tr: The hollows of the sacrum receive the tubers; the appendices and projecting parts of the sacrum enter the recesses.

units.la: Articulatio hæc, cum fine motu fit, Symphysis est.
units.tr: This joint, which has no motion, is called the symphysis.

units.la: Os pubis est anterior coxæ pars minus lata, utrumque amplum habens foramen.
units.tr: The pubic bone is the front part of the hip, less broad, having a large opening on each side.

units.la: Hujus ossa multæ cartilaginis inter-ventu tenacissimè coalescunt. Constituitur autem ex coxarum extremis anteriori parte coëuntibus.
units.tr: Its bones cohere very firmly by means of a considerable amount of cartilage. It is formed by the ends of the hips coming together at the front.

units.la: Estque hoc multò latius ac capacius in mulieribus, quàm viris.
units.tr: This is much wider and roomier in women than in men.

units.la: Quò magis autē deorsum tendunt, eò magis ac magis disjunguntur, ut vacuam sedem pudendis relinquant.
units.tr: But the further they extend downwards, the more and more they separate, so as to leave an empty seat for the private parts.

units.la: Os coxendicis est media coxę pars, angustior quidem, sed crassior extrinsecus, in magnum ac profundum sinum excisa.
units.tr: The hip-socket bone is the middle part of the hip, narrower indeed, but thicker on the outside, cut into a large and deep recess.

units.la: Hic sinus dicitur Acetabulum, in quod immittitur longum & rotundum femoris caput.
units.tr: This recess is called the acetabulum, into which the long and round head of the thigh-bone is inserted.

units.la: Exurgit ex hujus sinus labris crassa & circularis cartilago augens acetabuli capacitatem.
units.tr: From the rim of this recess rises a thick, circular cartilage, which enlarges the capacity of the socket.

units.la: SECTIO XI. DE FEMORE.
units.tr: SECTION XI. ON THE THIGH BONE.

units.la: Pedum ossa sunt Femur, & Crus.
units.tr: The bones of the foot are the thigh and the shin.

units.la: Femur est os pedis omnium maximum supra acetabulo coxendicis, infrà genu inarticulatum.
units.tr: The thigh bone is the largest of all the bones of the foot: above it is joined to the socket of the hip bone, and below, it is articulated with the knee.

units.la: Femoris caput est Superius & Inferius: utrumq; ex appendicibus supra infraq; huic osi adnatis formatum. Superius inseritur coxendici, habetq; quendam asperú sinum; (ceu teres ligamentum ex acetabulo prognatum implantatur.)
units.tr: The head of the thigh bone is the upper and the lower part, each formed from the projections that grow on this bone above and below. The upper part is inserted into the hip bone and has a certain rough hollow (where the round ligament, which grows out of the socket, is implanted, as it were).

units.la: Hujus capitis cervix est pars gracilior femoris capiti præposita.
units.tr: The neck of this head is the slenderer part of the thigh bone placed in front of the head.

units.la: Ab hac cervice os in portione quandam latiusculam descendit, ex qua processus duo veluti nodi educuntur, Rotatores dicti, quod rotando femori facti videantur.
units.tr: From this neck the bone descends into a somewhat broader portion, from which two processes stand out like knots, called the rotators, because they seem to have been made for rolling the thigh.

units.la: Inferius geminum est; quippe in duo magna capita diremtum medio sinu distincta.
units.tr: The lower part is double, since it is divided into two large heads separated by a central hollow.

units.la: Tendit autem à coxendice ad genu femur non recto tramite, sed cervix ejus primum oblique extrorsum à coxendice abscedit, ac deinde rursum oblique deorsum ad genu vergit.
units.tr: The thigh runs from the hip to the knee not in a straight course: its neck first leans obliquely outward away from the hip, and then again turns obliquely downward toward the knee.

units.la: SECTIO XII. DE PATELLA, TIBIA ET FIBULA.
units.tr: SECTIO XII. ON THE PATELLA, TIBIA AND FIBULA.

units.la: Crus est os pedis complectens ejus offa à femore ad imum usque.
units.tr: Crus is the bone of the leg, embracing its bones from the thigh down to the bottom.

units.la: Curvatura illa qua crus cum femore committitur, Genu dicitur.
units.tr: That curvature where the leg is joined to the thigh is called the knee.

units.la: Genu habet rotulam, quam Patellam vocant, quæ est os mobile, & orbiculare, instar scuti, tegendo femoris & cruris articulo præpositum,
units.tr: The knee has a kneecap, which they call the patella, a mobile, roundish bone like a shield, set in front to cover the joint of thigh and leg.

units.la: Patella cum femore articulatur per Ginglymon;
units.tr: The patella articulates with the femur by ginglymus.

units.la: Crurís ossa[?] sunt longa vel brevia.
units.tr: The bones of the leg are long or short.

units.la: Longa sunt dimensionis longæ inter femur & talum, ut Tibia & Fibula.
units.tr: The long ones are those of long extent between the thigh and the talus, such as the tibia and fibula.

units.la: Tibia est crassius & grandius os; altius ad femur ascendens.
units.tr: The tibia is the thicker and larger bone, rising higher up towards the thigh.

units.la: Habet autem infra supraq; appen-dicem.
units.tr: It has an appendage both below and above.

units.la: Ejus pars est Superior & Inferior.
units.tr: It has an upper and a lower part.

units.la: Superior pars tibiæ latior est & crassior, duos sinus leviter & in superficie sortita, inter quos est tuberculum quod-dam prominens & asperum.
units.tr: The upper part of the tibia is broader and thicker, having two shallow sinuses on its surface, between which is a certain prominent and rough tubercle.

units.la: A superiore hac parte deorsum proce-dens sensim attenuatur, longioribus li-neis ac finibus variis distincta, triangularem formam imitatur.
units.tr: From this upper part, proceeding downward, it gradually tapers, marked off by longer lines and various boundaries, and it imitates a triangular shape.

units.la: Inferior tibiæ pars rursum crassescit, & in caput definit, quod in superficie amplo sinu excisum tali insertionem exci-pit.
units.tr: The lower part of the tibia thickens again and ends in a head, which, hollowed on its surface by a wide notch, receives the insertion of the talus.

units.la: Hujus capitis pars interna in processum aliquanto crassum tendit, qui talum sinui inhærentem claudit.
units.tr: The inner part of this head extends into a somewhat thick process, which closes over the talus clinging to the notch.

units.la: Fibula est cruris os gracilius non tam altè ad femur ascendens, externæ tibiæ lateri infrà supraq; adnatum.
units.tr: The fibula is the slenderer bone of the leg, not rising so high towards the thigh, attached to the outer side of the tibia both below and above.

units.la: Proinde Fibulæ caput in acutum tendens tantò declivius ossè tibiæ descendit, quantùm tibiæ caput superius fibulam excedit,
units.tr: Accordingly, the head of the fibula, tapering to a point, descends along the bone of the shin the more steeply, by as much as the upper head of the tibia projects beyond the fibula.

units.la: Fibula infrà subit longum tibiæ sinum, facta conjunctione per Arthrodiam.
units.tr: The fibula below enters the long notch of the tibia, the joint being made by arthrodia.

units.la: Ambo fibulæ capita in processum acutum exeunt, quæ quibusdam asperitatibus sunt prædita.
units.tr: Both heads of the fibula end in a sharp process, and these are provided with certain roughnesses.

units.la: SECTIO XIII.
units.tr: SECTION XIII.

units.la: DE TARSO, ET PEDIO.
units.tr: CONCERNING THE TARSUS AND THE METATARSUS.

units.la: Ossa cruris brevia sunt extremi pedis ossa.
units.tr: The short bones of the leg are the bones of the extremity of the foot.

units.la: Suntq; conjuncta, velsejuncta.
units.tr: And they are either joined or disjoined.

units.la: Conjuncta pedis ossium intervenientibus utrinq; mediis copulata cohærent.
units.tr: The bones of the foot are joined when they are fastened together on both sides by intervening middle parts.

units.la: Suntq; Tarsus & Pedium.
units.tr: And these are the tarsus and the metatarsus.

units.la: Tarsus est septem ossium extremi pedis compositio, inter cruris ossa & pedium sita.
units.tr: The tarsus is the composition of seven bones of the extremity of the foot, situated between the bones of the leg and the bones of the toes.

units.la: Tarsi ossa sunt Nominata, vel Innominata.
units.tr: The bones of the tarsus are either named or unnamed.

units.la: Nominata sunt quatuor suo insignita nomine: Talus, Calx, Scaphoeides & Cyboeides.
units.tr: The named ones are four, each marked by its own name: the talus, the calcaneum, the scaphoid and the cuboid.

units.la: Talus est primum Tarsi os, rotulæ in medio sinum levé possidentis lateribus hinc inde prominentioribꝰ partem imitans, substratū tibiæ, in quo pes flectitur.
units.tr: The talus is the first bone of the tarsus, having in its middle a smooth hollow like a pulley, with prominences on either side, and forming the support of the tibia, on which the foot bends.

units.la: Hic tibiæ articulatur per ginglymon.
units.tr: Here it is jointed to the tibia by a hinge joint.

units.la: Isti autē semicirculari sinui inseritur media sese offerens calcis regio.
units.tr: Into this semicircular hollow is inserted the middle region of the calcaneum, presenting itself.

units.la: Calx seu Calcaneum est secundum tarsi os magnum tali ossi substratum, cujus latus internum insigniter excavatum est, externum vero depressum & inæquale.
units.tr: The calcaneum, or heel bone, is the second large bone of the tarsus, lying beneath the talus; its inner side is remarkably hollowed, while its outer side is depressed and uneven.

units.la: Scaphoeides seu naviforme est os tarsi tertium, in interna pedis parte positum, in anteriori sua sede oblongo sinu ob-longum caput tali recipiens.
units.tr: The scaphoid, or navicular bone, is the third bone of the tarsus, placed on the inner part of the foot; in its anterior seat, with an oblong hollow, it receives the oblong head of the talus.

units.la: Cyboeides seu cubiforme est quartum os tarsi, in extimo pedis latere jacens, parte anteriore cum calce junctum, posteri-ore vero duobus sinibus duo extrema pe-dii ossa suscipiens.
units.tr: The cuboid bone is the fourth bone of the tarsus, lying on the outer side of the foot; it is joined in front to the calcaneum, and behind it receives the two extremities of the two bones of the metatarsus with two hollows.

units.la: Innominata tarsi ossa sunt reliqua tria, è quibus duo ossi[?] naviformi, unum calcaneo inarticulatur.
units.tr: The unnamed bones of the tarsus are the remaining three, of which two are jointed to the navicular bone and one to the calcaneum.

units.la: ·Pedium est altera pars ossium pedis conjunctorum, prima parte crassa & sinuata, qua cum quatuor postremis tarsi ossibus componitur, altera cum primis digitorum articulis jungitur.
units.tr: The metatarsus is the other part of the bones of the foot joined together; its first part is thick and hollowed, by which it is articulated with the four rear bones of the tarsus, and its other part is joined to the first joints of the toes.

units.la: SECTIO XIV. DE OSSIBVS DIGITORVM PEDIS.
units.tr: SECTIO XIV. ON THE BONES OF THE TOES OF THE FOOT.

units.la: Sejuncta pedis extremi offa sunt, quæ ab utroq; latere separatim soluta sunt.
units.tr: The separate bones of the extremity of the foot are those which are loosened separately on either side.

units.la: Suntq; offa digitorum pedis, numero quatuordecim: singulis enim digitis terni sunt articuli, ut etiam in manu, excepto pollice pedis, cui duo tantùm obtigere.
units.tr: And the bones of the toes of the foot are fourteen in number: for each toe has three joints, as also in the hand, except the great toe of the foot, which has only two.

units.la: Hæc offa parùm discrepant ab ossibus digitorum manus, nisi quod internodia sui anteriore sinu constant profundiore, in quem inseruntur prominentiora ossium pedii capita: deinde internodia breviora sunt, quàm in ipsa manu, superne gibba, inferne vero sima.
units.tr: These bones differ little from the bones of the fingers of the hand, except that their intervals have a deeper hollow at the front, into which the more prominent heads of the bones of the foot are inserted; then the joints are shorter than in the hand itself, convex above and flat below.

units.la: Deniq; sub infimis digitorum pedis & manuum articulis depressa inter ipsa internodia jacentia inveniuntur orbicularia offa, quæ Sesamina vocant, quæ & propugnaculo sunt articulis, & infarciunt vacuum illud, quod iisdem articulis reliquum est. Hæc de ossibus.
units.tr: Finally, beneath the lowest joints of the toes of the foot and of the hands, small round bones are found lying depressed between the joints themselves, which they call sesamoid bones; these both protect the joints and fill up the empty space that remains in the same joints. So much for the bones.

units.la: CAPUT XXXIII: DE CARTILAGINE et Ligamento.
units.tr: CHAPTER XXXIII: ON CARTILAGE AND LIGAMENT.

units.la: Hactenus fuit osteologia in ossium enumeratione: Succedit se-cundi generis membrum, os sustinens, quod osse paulò mollius & humidius, ossibus ut plurimum annexum, membrorum aliorum fustentationem & continentiam seu cohærentiam juvat.
units.tr: So far we have had the osteology in the enumeration of the bones. There follows the second kind of member, the supporting member, which, being somewhat softer and moister than bone and mostly joined to the bones, helps with the support and the holding together or cohesion of the other members.

units.la: Estq; Cartilago vel Ligamentum.
units.tr: It is either cartilage or ligament.

units.la: Cartilago est membrum ad ossis naturam proxime accedens, præter sustentationem ossium commissuris præcipuè serviens.
units.tr: Cartilage is a member that comes very close to the nature of bone, serving chiefly to support the bones and to join them together at their junctions.

units.la: Hæc ut plurimum annexa est ossi; quædam enim cartilagines sunt solitariæ, non adnatæ ossibus, ut in ciliis oculorum, auriculis, larynge, aspera arteria.
units.tr: This is mostly attached to a bone; for some cartilages are solitary and not grown onto bones, as in the eyelashes, the ears, the larynx and the windpipe.

units.la: Cartilagines cum propria nomina non habeant, quibus distinguantur, partibus subjectis, quibus insunt & adhærent, differre possunt; possuntque aliæ dici capitis, aliæ trunci.
units.tr: Since cartilages do not have proper names by which they are distinguished, they can be differentiated by the parts beneath them to which they belong and adhere; and some can be called cartilages of the head, others of the trunk.

units.la: Capitis cum palpebrarum & aurium, tum nasi & inferioris maxillæ.
units.tr: Those of the head are the cartilages of the eyelids and of the ears, as well as of the nose and of the lower jaw.

units.la: Trunci cartilagines vel mediæ sunt, vel extremæ.
units.tr: The cartilages of the trunk are either middle or extreme.

units.la: Mediæ adhærent vel faucibus, vel trunci ossibus.
units.tr: The middle ones adhere either to the throat or to the bones of the trunk.

units.la: Ossibus trunci adhærent cartilagines dorsi, pectoris & lateris, ut cartilagines vertebrarum, sterni & costarum.
units.tr: To the bones of the trunk adhere the cartilages of the back, chest and side, such as the cartilages of the vertebrae, of the sternum and of the ribs.

units.la: Extremi trunci cartilagines sunt ossium vel excipientium, vel exceptorum.
units.tr: The extreme cartilages of the trunk belong to bones that either receive or are received.

units.la: Excipientium, ut scapulæ, vel coxæ.
units.tr: Those of the receiving bones are such as the shoulder-blade or the hip-socket.

units.la: Coxæ, ut coxendicis, vel ossium pubis.
units.tr: Those of the hip are such as those of the hip-joint or of the pubic bones.

units.la: Exceptorum sunt vel manus, vel pedum.
units.tr: Those of the received bones are either of the hand or of the foot.

units.la: Hæc de cartilaginibus. Mediam inter ossa & cartilagines naturam obtinent.
units.tr: So much for cartilages. They hold a nature intermediate between bones and cartilages.

units.la: Ungues, qui in extremitate digitorum cum manuum tum pedum extrinsecus adnati, non tam duri sunt ut ossa, neque tam molles ut cartilagines, ut mollissimam digitorum superficiem tueantur.
units.tr: Nails, which are attached externally at the tips of the fingers, both of the hands and of the feet, are not as hard as bones nor as soft as cartilages, so that they protect the very soft surface of the fingers.

units.la: Ligamentum seu vinculum ossi plerumque adhæret, cartilagine paulo mollius, tactui cedens, tenacius & viscosius, ossa præcipuè inter se, tum alia membra colligans & firmans.
units.tr: A ligament, or bond, is mostly attached to a bone; softer than cartilage, yielding to touch, tougher and more viscous, it binds and strengthens chiefly the bones among themselves, and also other members.

units.la: Oritur vel ex osse & cartilagine; vel membrana os circumdante.
units.tr: It arises either from bone and cartilage, or from a membrane surrounding the bone.

units.la: Ligamenta differunt pro ratione partium, earumq; varietate, quas colligant & continent.
units.tr: Ligaments differ according to the nature of the parts which they bind and hold together, and according to their variety.

units.la: CAPUT XXXIV. DE CUTE, ADIPE, ET MEMBRANA CARNOSA.
units.tr: CHAPTER XXXIV. CONCERNING THE SKIN, FAT, AND THE FLESHY MEMBRANE.

units.la: Actenus de membris sustentantibus: Sustentata sunt, quæ istis sustinentur, muniuntur & firmantur.
units.tr: So far concerning the supporting members. The supported parts are those which are sustained by these, protected and strengthened.

units.la: Sustentata sunt vel Involventia, vel Involuta.
units.tr: The supported parts are either enveloping or enveloped.

units.la: Involventia sunt aliorum membrorum naturalia & involventia tegumenta.
units.tr: The enveloping parts are the natural coverings and wrappings of the other members.

units.la: Involvens deinde membrum est universale, vel particulare.
units.tr: An enveloping member is then either universal or particular.

units.la: Universale est, quod universum corpus involvit, & tegit.
units.tr: The universal one is that which wraps and covers the whole body.

units.la: Estq; cutis, & membrana carnosa.
units.tr: This is the skin and the fleshy membrane.

units.la: Cutis est extimum universi corporis porosum involucrum.
units.tr: The skin is the porous outermost covering of the whole body.

units.la: Pori cutis sunt exigui & occultissimeatus tus fuliginosis liquidis & ferofis ultimæ concoctionis excrementis exitum præ-bentes. Ex hisce poris erumpunt etiam pili, qui ex viscidis recrementis, & vaporibus glutinosis ac fuliginosis calore ex-pulsis, ad corporis commodum ena-scuntur.
units.tr: The pores of the skin are small and very hidden passages, offering an exit to the sooty liquids and wild excretions of the final concoction. Through these pores also the hairs break forth, which grow for the good of the body from viscous residues and glutinous, sooty vapours driven out by heat.

units.la: Cutis partes sunt δέρμα καὶ ἐπιδερμίς.
units.tr: The parts of the skin are dermis [δέρμα] and epidermis [ἐπιδερμίς].

units.la: Δέρμα est vera cutis interior, crassa, sensus exquisitissimi, ex nervorum filamentis, venis & arteriis conflata.
units.tr: Dermis [δέρμα] is the true inner skin, thick, of the most exquisite sensation, made up of threads of nerves, veins and arteries.

units.la: Estque organum tactus propter nervos, extremitates suas ad hanc transmit-tentes.
units.tr: It is the organ of touch, because its nerves transmit their extremities to it.

units.la: Ἐπιδερμὶς seu cuticula est pars superfi-ciaria exiccata & tenuis medium tactus.
units.tr: The epidermis [ἐπιδερμίς], or cuticle, is the dry and thin outer part, the medium of touch.

units.la: Cuti subest plerunq; adeps, quæ suavis & mitis caloris ope, e sanguinis portione tenui, aerea & pingui per mufcu-lofam carnem transeunte, tandemque membranis illidente, & earum frigiditate (alii, soliditate:) concrescente, nasci-tur.
units.tr: Beneath the skin there is generally fat, which is produced, by the gentle and mild warmth, from a thin, airy and oily portion of the blood passing through the muscular flesh, and finally settling into the membranes, and congealing through their coldness (others say, through their firmness).

units.la: Membrana carnosa est universale involvens membrum, post cutem universum ambiens corpus.
units.tr: The fleshy membrane is the universal enveloping membrane, surrounding the whole body after the skin.

units.la: Huic membranæ subest & adhæret caro, quæ è sanguinis parte crassa, viscida & magis terrestri orta, spatia inter spermaticas fibras media infarcit
units.tr: Beneath and adhering to this membrane lies the flesh, which, arising from the thick, viscous and more earthy part of the blood, fills the spaces between the spermatic fibres.

units.la: Caput XXXV. De Membranis Nominatis & Innominatis.
units.tr: Chapter 35. On the Named and Unnamed Membranes.

units.la: Dhuc de involventibus universalibus: particulare involvens est, quod membra particularia & certa in corpore universo involvit:
units.tr: So far concerning the universal envelopes. A particular envelope is one that wraps particular and definite members within the whole body.

units.la: Estque membrana simplex, seu excarnis.
units.tr: It is either a membrane simply, or a skin without flesh.

units.la: MEMBRANA est particularium membrorum cute tenuius, densius, & siccius involucrum & tegumentum.
units.tr: A MEMBRANE is a covering and envelope of the particular members, thinner, denser and drier than the skin.

units.la: Membrana alia nomine insignita est, alia nomine caret.
units.tr: Some membranes are marked with a name, and some lack a name.

units.la: Membrana nomine insignita est, quæ præstantia corporis membra ambit & vestit.
units.tr: A named membrane is one that surrounds and clothes the principal members of the body.

units.la: Est autem ea ossium vel aliorum membrorum.
units.tr: These belong either to the bones or to other members.

units.la: Ossium membrana est propria unius, vel communis multis.
units.tr: The membrane of the bones is either proper to one bone or common to many.

units.la: Propria uni ossi tantum conveniens est PERICRANIUM.
units.tr: The membrane proper to one bone alone is the PERICRANIUM.

units.la: PERICRANIUM est membrana crá- nii seu calvariæ, externam convexamq; partem circumdans.
units.tr: The PERICRANIUM is the membrane of the skull or calvaria, surrounding its outer, convex part.

units.la: Communis ossibus reliquis involvendis communiter conveniens, dicitur PERI- OSTION.
units.tr: The membrane common to the remaining bones, which commonly serves to envelope them, is called the PERIOSTEUM.

units.la: Est autem PERIOSTION membra- na tenuis, ossa, quibus adhærescit vali- dè, multo sensu prædita, ambiens.
units.tr: The PERIOSTEUM is a thin membrane surrounding the bones to which it adheres firmly, and endowed with much sensation.

units.la: Hæc non spectatur in interna calva- riæ parte, neq; in dentibus.
units.tr: This is not found on the inner part of the calvaria, nor on the teeth.

units.la: Aliorum membrorum membranæ sunt vel multorum, vel singulorum.
units.tr: The membranes of the other members are either those of many or those of single members.

units.la: Multorum membrorum simul membra- næ involventes sunt Pleura, & Peritô- næum.
units.tr: The membranes that envelop several members at once are the Pleura and the Peritoneum.

units.la: PLEURA seu tunica costas succin- gens, est membrana universam interio- ris thoracis superficie integens, & omnia membra thoracis concavo complexa.
units.tr: The PLEURA, or the tunic girding the ribs, is the membrane covering the whole inner surface of the chest and enfolding all the members of the chest in its concavity.

units.la: Estq; duarum partium; nimirum in- ternæ & externæ.
units.tr: It has two parts, namely the internal and the external.

units.la: Pleura repens deorsum juxta later a Sterni, versus spinam, & inter se dextr- à sinistra distans, Spinæ affixa, thoracem in duas cavitates secans, ibi Mediastinum dicitur.
units.tr: The pleura, creeping downward beside the sides of the sternum toward the spine, and separated from its counterpart on the right and left, attached to the spine and dividing the chest into two cavities, is there called the mediastinum.

units.la: Mediastinum ergo est duplicata membrana, à pleura progrediens, thoracem medians à summo thorace ad imum usque ducta.
units.tr: The mediastinum, then, is a doubled membrane, proceeding from the pleura, dividing the chest and drawn from the top of the chest to the bottom.

units.la: Peritonæum est membrana omnibus iis membris & vasis, quæ ventris inferioris & abdominis cavitate continentur, circumtensa.
units.tr: The peritoneum is the membrane stretched around all those members and vessels that are contained in the cavity of the lower belly and abdomen.

units.la: Ex peritonæo circa duodecimam vertebram thoracis sub ipso ventriculo oritur Omentum.
units.tr: From the peritoneum, near the twelfth vertebra of the chest, beneath the stomach itself, arises the omentum.

units.la: Est autem Omentum membrana tenuis ac levis, abundans multis venis, arteriis & nervis, atque adipe copiosa, nonnulla etiam ubique glandulosa carne, substratum intestinis, ut innatare quasi videantur.
units.tr: The omentum is a thin and light membrane, abounding in many veins, arteries and nerves, and in copious fat, and in some places also in glandular flesh, lying beneath the intestines so that they seem almost to float.

units.la: Singulorum membrorum nominata membrana sunt vel cerebri, vel cordis.
units.tr: The named membranes of single members are those of the brain or of the heart.

units.la: Cerebrum amplectens membrana Meninx dicitur; panniculus scilicet totam cerebri molem involvens.
units.tr: The membrane enclosing the cerebrum is called the meninx, namely the covering that wraps the whole mass of the brain.

units.la: Meninx est crassa, vel tenera.
units.tr: The meninx is either thick or tender.

units.la: Crassa meninx vulgo dicitur dura mater, & est membrana crassa, crânio proximá, xima, tenerae meningi obducta, à Pericranio ligamentis per futuras porrectis suspensa.
units.tr: The thick meninx is commonly called the dura mater; it is a thick membrane lying nearest the skull, covered over the tender meninx, and hung from the pericranium by ligaments extended through the sutures.

units.la: Tenera meninx vulgo Pia mater est tenuissima membrana proximè & immediatè cerebrum involvens, crassæ meningi subjecta.
units.tr: The tender meninx, commonly the pia mater, is a very thin membrane closely and immediately enveloping the brain, lying beneath the thick meninx.

units.la: Cordis membrana dicitur Pericardion.
units.tr: The membrane of the heart is called the pericardium.

units.la: Pericardion seu Capsula cordis est membrana crassa & dura, validis ligamentis in sua sede contenta, circumquaq; cordi æquali distantia circumducta, ne quid cor premat & motum ejus impediat.
units.tr: The pericardium, or capsule of the heart, is a thick and hard membrane, held in its place by strong ligaments, drawn around the heart on all sides at an equal distance, so that nothing presses the heart and impedes its motion.

units.la: In hujus pericardii fundo Humor quidam aqueus est, quo cor perpetuò in isto motu humectatur.
units.tr: In the bottom of this pericardium there is a certain watery humour, by which the heart is constantly moistened in its motion.

units.la: Innominata membrana, sunt, quæ reliqua quædam membra includunt & vestiunt, nec sunt nomen sortitæ[?].
units.tr: The unnamed membranes are those which enclose and clothe certain other members and have obtained no name.

units.la: CAPUT XXXVI. DE SEMINE HUMANO ET SANGUINE MENSTRUO, generationis principiis.
