units.tr: The internal and proper sensory organ of smell consists of two nervous or mammillary ducts, rising from the middle breadth of the brain, not from the spinal marrow, and descending to the uppermost nostrils. Through these ducts the animal spirits carry the odours to the brain, which, being moist, could easily be affected by the odorous exhalation that continually flows out from the odorous body; and since a scented vapour tends to spread more widely the farther it travels from its source, the whole brain is to be credited with this, lest it be suffocated, shut up in a narrow vessel.

units.la: Exterius organum est Nasus, per quem portio attracti aëris odora, ceu caminum perflat.
units.tr: The external organ is the nose, through which a portion of the inhaled air, laden with odour, blows as through a chimney.

units.la: Hic longus est, ut aliquo modo in ea cavitate aër deferens incalesceret.
units.tr: It is long, so that the air carried into that cavity may be warmed in some measure.

units.la: Inferius latus est, superius vero angustus, ut facile odores suscipiercentur; suscepti vero majori cum impetu in cerebrum illaberentur: In summitate enim os residet crebris foraminibus cribrosum.
units.tr: It is wide below and narrow above, so that the odours may be taken in easily; and once taken in, they would glide into the brain with greater force, for at the top sits the bone, perforated with many holes like a sieve.

units.la: Opem huic delationi ferunt Musculi, qui à superiori Maxilla prodeuntes, alas narium arripiunt, aperiunt, & apertas conservant.
units.tr: The muscles lend help to this passage: they arise from the upper jaw, seize the wings of the nostrils, open them, and keep them open once opened.

units.la: CAPUT LIV. DE MEMBRIS RESPIRATIONIS: QUARUM PLERAQUE serviunt facultati Sermocinatrici.
units.tr: CHAPTER 54. ON THE MEMBERS OF RESPIRATION, MOST OF WHICH SERVE THE FACULTY OF SPEECH.

units.la: Hactenus de membris facultatis sen-sitricis, & quidem sensuum exteri-orum. Membra & organa facultatis Motricis sunt, per quæ facultas animalis motus animales in corpore ciet.
units.tr: So far concerning the members of the sensitive faculty, and indeed of the external senses. The members and organs of the motive faculty are those through which the faculty of animal motion produces animal movements in the body.

units.la: Suntq; motricis vel ζωϊκῆς[?], vel αἰσθη-τικῆς[?] organa.
units.tr: And there are organs of the motive faculty that are either vital [ζωϊκῆς] or sensitive [αἰσθητικῆς].

units.la: Motricis ζωϊκῆς seu vitalis sunt vel Respiratricis vel Micatricis facultatis membra.
units.tr: The members of the vital or life-giving motive faculty are either those of the respiratory faculty or of the pulsatile faculty.

units.la: Respirationis organa sunt, quæ famulantur aëris in corpus inspirationi & expirationi.
units.tr: The organs of respiration are those which serve the intake and outflow of air into and out of the body.

units.la: Suntq; duorum generum. Primi generis sunt Diaphragma, & Pulmo.
units.tr: And they are of two kinds. The members of the first kind are the diaphragm and the lung.

units.la: DIAPHRAGMA, est quasi continuus musculꝰ in medio nerveus, in circuitu carneus, utrinq; membranis vestitus, inter thoracem & ventrem inferiorem situs, quo contracto thorax dilatatur, & fit inspiratio, laxato vero thorax in se concidit, & fit expiratio.
units.tr: The DIAPHRAGM is a kind of continuous muscle, nervous in its middle and fleshy around its edge, clothed on both sides with membranes, situated between the chest and the lower belly. When it contracts, the chest is widened and inspiration occurs; when it relaxes, the chest collapses in upon itself and expiration occurs.

units.la: Pulmo est membrum respirationis spongiosum, rarum, molle, spumæ sanguinis concretæ simile, in spacio supremo thoracis ad dexteram nonnihil inclinans, quo dilatato, aër attrahitur, attracto vero, idem redditur.
units.tr: The LUNG is a spongy, porous, soft member of respiration, like concreted foam of blood, lying in the upper space of the chest and leaning somewhat to the right. When it expands, air is drawn in; when it is drawn in, the same air is given back.

units.la: Pulmo autè membrana per medium diremtus habet partem dexteram & si-nistram: utraq; binis lobis insignita.
units.tr: The lung, however, is divided through the middle by a membrane into a right and a left part, each marked by two lobes.

units.la: Secundi generis membra respirationis sunt vasa deferentia aerem, uti est TRA-CHEA ARTERIA.
units.tr: The members of the second kind of respiration are the vessels that convey the air, such as the windpipe, the trachea artery.

units.la: ASPERA ARTERIA est canalis re-spirationis linguae radici annexus, e multis semicirculis cartilagineis in parte anteriore gutturis continuata serie, ex membranis vero ea parte, qua respicit æsophagum, constructus, diffusus in substantiam pulmonum, eiq; spiritum seu aerem afferens.
units.tr: The ASPERA ARTERIA (windpipe) is a channel of respiration joined to the root of the tongue, made of many cartilaginous half-rings in a continuous series along the front of the throat, and constructed of membranes on the side facing the gullet; it spreads out into the substance of the lungs and carries breath or air to them.

units.la: Tracheæ arterię summum caput seu orificium dicitur LARYNX, quod ex tribus cartilaginibus, duabus extimis, tertia vero inter has media, constat, vo-ci edendæ famulans.
units.tr: The uppermost head or opening of the windpipe is called the LARYNX, which consists of three cartilages, two outer and a third in the middle between them, and serves for producing the voice.

units.la: Laryngi adjungitur cum GLOTTIS, tum EPIGLOTTIS.
units.tr: To the larynx are joined both the GLOTTIS and the EPIGLOTTIS.

units.la: Glottis est rima in medio laryngis, potissimum vocis formandæ instrumen-tum.
units.tr: The glottis is the slit in the middle of the larynx, chiefly the instrument for forming the voice.

units.la: Epiglottis est operculum cartilagine-um tegens rimam, in respiratione aeri cedens, in deglutiendo rimam clau-dens.
units.tr: The epiglottis is a cartilaginous lid covering the slit, yielding to the air in breathing and closing the slit in swallowing.

units.la: CAPUT LV. DE CORDE, ET ARTERIIS.
units.tr: CHAPTER 55. ON THE HEART AND THE ARTERIES.

units.la: Sic fuerunt membra respirationis: Organa Micationis sunt, quibus motus micationis, & pulsus perficitur.
units.tr: Such are the members of respiration. There are also the organs of pulsation, by which the motion of the pulse and the beat are carried out.

units.la: Micationis membra sunt Cor, & Arteria; hic pulsus magis proprius dicitur.
units.tr: The members of the pulse are the heart and the artery; the latter is more properly called the pulse.

units.la: Cor est primarium membrum micationis, in thorace & medio corporis suspensum, carnosum, probeque compactum, figurae pyramidalis, officina caloris & spiritus vitalis per totum corpus distribuendi.
units.tr: The heart is the chief member of the pulse. It lies in the chest and in the middle of the body, is fleshy and well compacted, pyramidal in shape, and is the workshop for distributing heat and vital spirit throughout the whole body.

units.la: Cordis sunt cum Ventriculi, tum Auriculae.
units.tr: The heart has both ventricles and auricles.

units.la: Ventriculi, sinus seu thalami cordis sunt insignes cavitates, cordi insculptae, interna parte multa inaequalitate & asperitate donatae, in quibus spiritus & sanguis arteriosus elaboratur.
units.tr: The ventricles, or sinuses and chambers of the heart, are notable cavities carved into the heart, their inner part having great unevenness and roughness, and in them the spirit and arterial blood are prepared.

units.la: In his ventriculis sunt orificia, quibus praesident membranea ostiola, quae ut unumquodq; tantum, quatenus opus est ingrediatur in eos, & ex iis egrediatur, cordis orificia obstruunt & referant.
units.tr: At these ventricles there are openings, guarded by membranous valves, which open and close the orifices of the heart, so that each lets in and out only as much as is needed.

units.la: Ventriculi cordis sunt duo, dexter & sinister.
units.tr: The ventricles of the heart are two: the right and the left.

units.la: Dexter ventriculus cordis est in dextra parte ejus magis, quodammodo deorsum ad cordis mucronem, instar falcatae Lunae vergens, sanguinem receptum e-laboratius excoquens, & extenuans suo calore.
units.tr: The right ventricle of the heart lies more on the right side, leaning somewhat downward toward the apex of the heart, shaped like a sickle moon; it cooks the received blood more thoroughly and thins it by its heat.

units.la: In dextrum cordis Thalamum infigitur vena cava, & vena arterialis, illa sanguinem ex epate affert; haec coctum jam e corde in pulmones effert.
units.tr: Into the right chamber of the heart are inserted the vena cava and the venous artery: the former brings blood from the liver, the latter carries it, already cooked, from the heart into the lungs.

units.la: Sinister ventriculus (qui tamen in medio cordis conspicitur) instar coni ar-ctum versus mucronem paulatim desinens, officina & promtuariu[?] est spirituum vitalium.
units.tr: The left ventricle (which nevertheless is seen in the middle of the heart) tapers gradually into a narrow shape like a cone toward the apex; it is the workshop and storehouse of the vital spirits.

units.la: E sinistro ventriculo oritur cum ar-teria aorta, tum arteria venalis.
units.tr: From the left ventricle arise both the aorta and the arterial vein.

units.la: Illa arteriarum truncus maximus e corde arteriosum sanguinem & spiritum vitalem excipit & evehit: haec dicitur aërem extrinsecus advenientem e pulmonibus in sinistrum ventriculum transmittere.
units.tr: The aorta, the greatest trunk of the arteries, receives from the heart the arterial blood and vital spirit and carries them out; the other is said to transmit the air coming in from outside, from the lungs, into the left ventricle.

units.la: Hi ventriculi distinguuntur medio septo satis crasso, multisq; foraminibus pervio,per quę sanguis spirituosus è dextro in sinistrum transsudat.
units.tr: These ventricles are separated by a middle partition, fairly thick and pierced by many pores, through which the spirituous blood seeps from the right into the left.

units.la: Auricula cordis sunt notabiles cavitates, utrinq; ad basin cordis in superiora ventriculorum definentes, quæ suo peculiari motu aërem ad spiritus refocillationem & caloris eventationem ad se trahere dicuntur.
units.tr: The auricles of the heart are notable cavities on either side at the base of the heart, reaching up to the upper parts of the ventricles; by their own peculiar motion they are said to draw air to themselves for refreshing the spirits and fanning the heat.

units.la: Tota hæc cordis fabrica involuta est pericardio seu capsulę cordis, aquam, sua humectatione faciliorem cordis motum reddentem, continenti.
units.tr: This whole structure of the heart is enclosed in the pericardium, or capsule of the heart, which holds water that, by moistening it, makes the motion of the heart easier.

units.la: ARTERIA est secundum micatio-nis & pulsus proprium membrum, vas scilicet concavum crassiusculum, è corde ortum, spiritum vitalem una cum sanguine arterioso, cordis nimirum calore & motu, pulmonumque agitatione elaborato & extenuato, adeoque calorem influentę per omnes corporis partes diffundens.
units.tr: The ARTERY is the member proper to the beat and pulse: namely a fairly thick hollow vessel, arising from the heart, which diffuses the vital spirit, prepared and thinned together with the arterial blood by the heat and motion of the heart and the agitation of the lungs, and so spreads heat through all parts of the body.

units.la: CAPUT LVI. DE MUSCULIS.
units.tr: CHAPTER 56. ON THE MUSCLES.

units.la: Superest organum Motricis αἰσθητικῆς[?] & sensum insequentis, & quidem externæ Locomotivæ, quod dicitur Musculus.
units.tr: There remains the organ of the motive faculty (αἰσθητικῆς [?]) and the follower of sense, and indeed of the external locomotive faculty, which is called the muscle.

units.la: Est autem Musculus motricis facultatis sensum insequentis & voluntarie instrumentum, constans ex nervis, fibris, ligamentis, carne fibras implente, venis & arteriis, & cingente panniculo, mire sibi invicem intertextis.
units.tr: A muscle is the instrument of the motive faculty that follows sense and acts voluntarily. It consists of nerves, fibres, ligaments, flesh filling the fibres, veins and arteries, and an enclosing membrane, all wonderfully interwoven with one another.

units.la: Partes musculi sunt Caput, Venter & Cauda. Caput musculi, est anterior pars, quae ligamentis, venis, arteriis & nervis maxime abundat.
units.tr: The parts of the muscle are the head, the belly and the tail. The head of the muscle is the front part, which abounds most in ligaments, veins, arteries and nerves.

units.la: Venter, est media pars musculi, maxime carnosa.
units.tr: The belly is the middle part of the muscle, which is most fleshy.

units.la: Cauda, est posterior musculi pars, e ligamentis & nervis conflata, dicitur{que} chorda.
units.tr: The tail is the back part of the muscle, made up of ligaments and nerves, and it is called the chorda.

units.la: CHORDA igitur est voluntarii motus immediatum & proximum instrumentum, quod tractum, ipsum membrum movendum trahit & movet.
units.tr: The CHORDA, therefore, is the immediate and proximate instrument of voluntary motion: when drawn, it pulls and moves the very member that is to be moved.

units.la: FINIS.
units.tr: THE END.

units.la: Deo naturae opifici sit gloria.
units.tr: Let the glory be to God, the Maker of nature.
